findings.title: Successful cache deletion does not refresh the connected-calendars query
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback, unlike the disconnect mutation below it which invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars on settle. In SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper the internal suspense query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt is therefore not refetched (onChanged is an optional external callback and may be undefined), so after a successful deletion the dropdown keeps showing the old timestamp and 'Delete cached data' action until a manual reload.

findings.title: Cache status ignores expiry and reports dead cache entries as live
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows for the credentials without filtering expiresAt, while getCachedAvailability only serves rows with expiresAt >= now and entries expire after CACHING_TIME (30 days). A credential whose cache expired long ago is therefore reported to the UI as having a current cache with a 'Last updated' timestamp and a delete action, even though that cache is never used.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId accepts the wrong Prisma input type
findings.body: The method types its data parameter as Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, which is the single-record update type and permits nested relation operations, but forwards it to prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany, which only accepts scalar SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput fields. Callers that pass relation data allowed by this signature will fail Prisma validation at runtime; the signature should use the update-many mutation input type (and the sole caller in CalendarService.ts passes {} relying on implicit @updatedAt behaviour rather than an explicit updatedAt value).

findings.title: Committed webhook test script is macOS-only and writes outside the repo
findings.body: This unrelated dev script uses `sed -i ''`, which is BSD/macOS syntax and fails under GNU sed on Linux, and it resolves ENV_FILE as '../.env' relative to the caller's working directory rather than the script/repo root, so running it from the repo root edits a .env file outside the repository. Its cleanup() also exits 0 even when no tunnel URL was obtained (lines 56-59), masking failures from callers.

findings.title: dev:cron now depends on an unpinned npx download
findings.body: The unrelated change replaces ts-node with `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` without adding tsx to devDependencies. Every run may download the latest unpinned tsx from the network, making the script fail offline and non-reproducible/supply-chain sensitive; tsx should be pinned as a devDependency (invoked via yarn) or the change dropped from this PR.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is always formatted in en-US regardless of user locale
findings.body: The 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...) even though the component already uses useLocale for translations. Non-US users will see US date/time ordering and conventions instead of formatting in their configured locale.

findings.title: No tests for the new cache deletion authorization or cache-status query
findings.body: This PR adds a new destructive, ownership-checked mutation (deleteCacheHandler) and a new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds repository query consumed by connectedCalendarsHandler, but includes no tests at all. There is no coverage proving a user cannot delete another user's cache by credentialId, that deletion removes only that credential's rows, or that cacheUpdatedAt is mapped to the correct credential, so an authorization or mapping regression would ship undetected.
